clue.text: Kind of person that gives generous help to the needy

definitions.text: that gives generous help to the needy

parts.note: kind means benevolent, generous to others
body is an informal word for a person, as in 'a cheerful old body'

explanation.surface: Describing the sort of person who is generous to those in need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of person' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two pieces, with 'of' only joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation set up to aid the poor is a registered charity, the body that gives help.

clue.text: A vessel of rude construction promised security

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel

indicators.note: a construction is something built up from parts, so these letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A roughly built boat nonetheless guaranteed safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' rebuilds RUDE as URED, which follows A and SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone assured has been guaranteed something, given a pledge of safety or insurance cover.

clue.text: He be butter-like and I be cross

parts.note: taken as written
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Two speakers in dialect compare themselves, one gentle as butter, one angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter-like' does not mean soft: a butter here is something that butts, as a wild mountain goat does with its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild goat of the Alps butts with its great curved horns, so a male one is a butter.

clue.text: Yet a turn-up restrains rent solicitor

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so one piece is held inside the other
in a down clue a turn-up flips the words above it, so they are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
rent, past tense of rend, means torn

explanation.surface: An unexpected event means a lawyer is unable to collect the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a turn-up' reverses YET A to ATEY, and 'restrains' holds TORN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a lawyer, and in Britain someone formally appointed to act for another in law.

clue.text: Knock-down sales I miss north of the border

indicators.note: knocking something down scatters it, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Cut-price sales that a shopper regrets missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north of the border' means in Scotland, where a young girl, a miss, is a lassie.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a girl or young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Slim 1.opportunity to strip?

parts.note: a slim opportunity is a scant one, and read another way it is a chance to get naked

explanation.surface: Someone sees a narrow chance to undress.
explanation.walkthrough: The '1.' printed after 'Slim' is a scanning stray, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bare chance is a very small likelihood; being bare is also being undressed.

clue.text: Did gong get justified for taking evasive action?

indicators.note: justified text has its letters realigned, so these letters are lined up afresh

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether their medal was deserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for a medal, which drives the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging is avoiding a blow or duty by quick movement, moving aside to escape.

clue.text: Perhaps the Bailey gang making rival bids for con tracts

definitions.text: making rival bids for con tracts

parts.note: a Bailey bridge is a prefabricated military bridge, so it is one example of a bridge
a gang is a party or group

explanation.surface: The Bailey gang of fraudsters compete over swindles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con tracts' is 'contracts' split: a gathering of card players bidding contracts. 'the Bailey' suggests the Old Bailey, London's criminal court, but the Bailey is a portable bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: At a card gathering of this game, players bid against one another to win contracts.

clue.text: Confused Mayday message beats friend of 12 fighters

indicators.note: confused things are mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal, as is Mayday

explanation.surface: A panicked distress call beats off rescuers.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is FIRE, so '12 fighters' are firefighters, whose protective suits were once made of this fireproof mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral resists heat, so it served in protective clothing for those battling blazes.

clue.text: Taken aback; extra clause added

definitions.meaning: carried on a back, as a jockey is by a horse
an amendment tacked on to a bill or contract

explanation.definitionFit: A horseman is borne on a horse's back, and an addendum to a document has the same name.

clue.text: When working classes must do prep for tomorrow

definitions.text: When working classes must do prep for tomorrow

parts.words: When working classes must do prep for tomorrow
parts.note: reads like the labouring class getting ready, but means the time pupils do homework once lessons end

explanation.surface: The labouring classes must prepare for the next day.
explanation.definitionFit: Once lessons finish, pupils do homework (prep) in the period following the day's teaching.

clue.text: Order of the bullet

definitions.meaning: to get the bullet is to be sacked from a job

explanation.definitionFit: The command to shoot a gun, and dismissal from employment, both share this word.

clue.text: The issue of some inventive thought

definitions.text: The issue of some inventive thought

parts.words: The issue of some inventive thought
parts.note: issue means offspring, so this is a child born of the mind

explanation.surface: Discussing the result of creative thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: An original idea is spoken of as the offspring of the mind that conceived it.

clue.text: Creations of Nature drew no breath here

indicators.note: a creation is a thing made from material, so these letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Nature's creatures never breathed in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Below the surface of the sea a person cannot take in air.

clue.text: Archer has new green belt put at risk

indicators.note: to belt is to encircle, as a belt does a waist, so one piece goes around the other
new tells us the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: Dan Archer was a leading character in The Archers, the long-running BBC radio farming soap

explanation.surface: A bowman has a fresh green girdle and is placed in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns GREEN into ENGER, which 'belt' wraps round DAN. The Archers is a British radio soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil something is to expose it to danger or harm.

clue.text: Baby horse in high wind makes for a lot of goose flesh

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A foal out in a storm gets goosebumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goose flesh' looks like goosebumps; it means geese in a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock of geese on the ground is called by this collective noun.

clue.text: Devilish disposition of a fallen saint in write-up

indicators.note: a fallen saint has been toppled, so these letters are tumbled
in a down clue up means the piece reads from the bottom

parts.note: MS, a manuscript, is something written

explanation.surface: A saint who has fallen into sin writes about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fallen' turns A SAINT into SATANI, and 'up' turns MS into SM.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of Satan is a devoted inclination toward evil.

clue.text: Repast for prince in marvellous surroundings

indicators.note: one piece forms the surroundings of the other

parts.note: super means marvellous

explanation.surface: A meal fit for royalty in splendid setting.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening meal, a repast taken late in the day.

clue.text: 19 A mount to appeal to a flying 10?

definitions.text: A mount to appeal to a flying 10?

parts.words: A mount to appeal to a flying 10?
parts.note: 10 is RIDER, so a flying rider would want a horse that flies

explanation.surface: Seeking a steed fit for a jockey who travels at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading '19' is the clue number scanned into the text.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged horse of Greek myth would suit a horseman who wants to go airborne.

clue.text: A month by sea arranged for noble lady abroad

parts.note: March is a month

indicators.note: arranged things are set in order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A month's sea voyage is organised for an aristocratic woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title for a marquis's wife, a noblewoman of that rank.

clue.text: Without end alien learnt about English

indicators.note: something alien is strange, so these letters are made strange by rearranging

explanation.surface: Endlessly a foreigner learns about the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alien' turns LEARNT into TERNAL; 'about' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting has no finish in time.

clue.text: Fictitious dragon flies

parts.note: dragonflies are insects, but here a legendary dragon takes to the air

explanation.definitionFit: A two-legged winged beast of heraldry and legend, a mythical dragon that flies.

clue.text: Many a hold up caused by such a road worker

definitions.text: Many a hold up caused by such a road worker

parts.words: Many a hold up caused by such a road worker
parts.note: a road worker causes traffic delays, but this man on the road robbed travellers

explanation.surface: Roadworks and their workers cause many traffic jams.
explanation.walkthrough: A hold-up is both a traffic delay and an armed robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounted robber worked the main roads, stopping coaches to rob them.

clue.text: A tough grass, or criminal?

definitions.meaning: a wiry type of grass with stiff stems
British slang for corrupt or dishonest

explanation.definitionFit: A stiff-stemmed grass species, and a slang term for crooked, describing a dishonest police officer.

clue.text: He edified young Victorians in clerical garb

indicators.note: the name lies inside the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A clergyman in his vestments improved the morals of Victorian youth.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric, or Little by Little was an improving Victorian school story by Dean Farrar.
explanation.definitionFit: The title boy of Farrar's moralising novel was a model to instruct young readers.

clue.text: Where the film extras gathered for attack

definitions.meaning: extras gather on a film set
an attack is an assault or a sudden beginning

explanation.definitionFit: Film performers gather at the studio location, and an assault is also a beginning of hostilities.

clue.text: One who leaves on record company expenses

parts.note: EMI is a well-known British record company
a grant is money allowed to meet expenses

explanation.surface: A recording artist goes on the record label's expense account.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone departing their homeland to settle abroad.

clue.text: Miss the starter appertaining to good food appreciation almost incalculably

indicators.note: the starter is the first letter, which is left out

parts.note: gastronomy is the appreciation of fine food

explanation.surface: Skipping the first course at a gourmet meal costs an enormous amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course of a meal, but here it is the first letter, which is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Star distances are enormous, so in a manner beyond reckoning means vastly.
